title: Thick generation of a fully faithful exact essential image
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Assume $\mathcal C$ is idempotent complete, meaning that for every $e:X\to X$ with $e^2=e$ there are $Y$, $i:Y\to X$, $r:X\to Y$ with $ri=1_Y$ and $ir=e$. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an exact fully faithful functor (its maps on morphism sets are bijective, it commutes coherently with integer shifts, and it sends distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles). Let $G$ be a class of objects of $\mathcal C$. A thick subcategory means a strictly full subcategory containing zero and closed under integer shifts, extensions in distinguished triangles and retracts; a retract of $X$ is an object $Y$ with maps $i:Y\to X$, $r:X\to Y$ satisfying $ri=1_Y$. Suppose the smallest thick subcategory of $\mathcal C$ containing $G$ is $\mathcal C$ itself. Then the essential image $\{Y\in\mathcal D:\exists X\in\mathcal C,\ Y\cong F(X)\}$ is a thick subcategory of $\mathcal D$, and it equals the smallest thick subcategory of $\mathcal D$ containing $\{F(g):g\in G\}$. No smallness assumption on the class $G$ and no idempotent-completeness assumption on $\mathcal D$ are imposed.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal I$ for the essential image, as a strictly full subcategory. It is closed under isomorphisms by composing the isomorphisms in its definition. Exactness includes additivity [def-weil-triangulated-category], so $1_{F(0)}=F(1_0)=F(0)=0$; composing any morphism to or from $F(0)$ with this identity shows it is zero, so $F(0)$ is a zero object. Thus $0\in\mathcal I$. If $Y\cong F(X)$, then $Y[n]\cong F(X)[n]\cong F(X[n])$ for every integer $n$, using the given coherent shift isomorphisms. Thus $\mathcal I$ is shift-stable.

source.place: First paragraph and complement: closure operations on the comparison image; elementary verification of zero, isomorphisms and shifts.

proof.text: We check cone closure, including the comparison map. Given a distinguished triangle $A\xrightarrow{u}B\to C\to A[1]$ in $\mathcal D$ with isomorphisms $s:F(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ and $t:F(Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}B$, fullness lifts $t^{-1}us$ to $f:X\to Y$. By TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] choose a distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\to Z\to X[1]$. Its image is distinguished by exactness of $F$. Since $tF(f)=us$, TR3 gives a morphism from this image triangle to the given triangle with first two components $s,t$. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], its third component $F(Z)\to C$ is an isomorphism. Hence $C\in\mathcal I$. For extension closure, if instead $A,C\in\mathcal I$ in the original triangle, rotate twice by TR2 to get the distinguished triangle $C\to A[1]\to B[1]\to C[1]$ (with the prescribed rotation signs on its last two arrows). The first two vertices are in $\mathcal I$, so cone closure gives $B[1]\in\mathcal I$ and shift stability gives $B\in\mathcal I$.

source.place: Tags 0145 and 05QL (definition-triangulated-category and definition-exact-functor); Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle. The TR1/TR3 argument is the proof of Tag 014B, lemma-cone-triangle-unique-isomorphism, applied with the displayed endpoint isomorphisms.

proof.text:
For retract closure it suffices, after replacing an object by its specified image isomorphism, to take $i:Y\to F(X)$, $r:F(X)\to Y$ with $ri=1_Y$. Put $e=ir$. Then $e^2=e$. Fullness gives $p:X\to X$ with $F(p)=e$, and faithfulness gives $p^2=p$. Idempotent completeness of $\mathcal C$, in exactly the splitting form assumed in the statement, gives $a:X'\to X$, $b:X\to X'$ with $ba=1_{X'}$, $ab=p$. Define $\alpha=F(b)i:Y\to F(X')$ and $\beta=rF(a):F(X')\to Y$. Directly,
$$\alpha\beta=F(b)eF(a)=F(baba)=1_{F(X')},\qquad \beta\alpha=rF(ab)i=re i=riri=1_Y.$$
Thus $Y\cong F(X')$ belongs to $\mathcal I$. Together with the preceding steps this proves that $\mathcal I$ is thick. This uses a splitting only in $\mathcal C$, never one in $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Tag 09SH, lemma-karoubian: splitting criterion for idempotents. Here a splitting is already a hypothesis, and the lifting and inverse equations are an elementary calculation.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal S$ be any thick subcategory of $\mathcal D$ containing every $F(g)$, $g\in G$. Its full inverse image has object class $\mathcal P=\{X\in\mathcal C:F(X)\in\mathcal S\}$. Functors preserve isomorphisms; step 1 gives $F(0)\cong0$ and the shift comparisons; and exactness [def-weil-triangulated-category] sends a distinguished triangle to a distinguished triangle. These facts and the defining closure properties of $\mathcal S$ show that $\mathcal P$ is strictly full, contains zero, and is stable under integer shifts and extensions. If $ri=1_Y$ exhibits $Y$ as a retract of $X$ in $\mathcal C$, then $F(r)F(i)=1_{F(Y)}$, so $F(Y)\in\mathcal S$ whenever $F(X)\in\mathcal S$. Thus $\mathcal P$ is thick and contains $G$. The generation hypothesis implies $\mathcal P=\mathcal C$. Consequently every $F(X)$, and then every object isomorphic to one, is in $\mathcal S$, so $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal S$.

source.place: Complement, final thick-generation conclusion: inverse-image argument for the minimal thick subcategory, written out for an arbitrary thick subcategory.

proof.text: Every $F(g)$ belongs to $\mathcal I$ by its definition. The first three steps show that $\mathcal I$ is thick, and step 4 shows that it is contained in every thick subcategory containing these images. This is precisely the defining minimality of the smallest thick subcategory containing $\{F(g):g\in G\}$. Hence that subcategory equals $\mathcal I$. The argument quantifies over an arbitrary class $G$ and an arbitrary thick subcategory; it never forms a coproduct indexed by $G$ or assumes $G$ is small.

lean.statement: theorem essImage_thick_eq_triangEnvelope {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C] [∀ (n : ℤ), (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated C] {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D] [∀ (n : ℤ), (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D] [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated D] [IsIdempotentComplete C] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Full] [F.Faithful] [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] (G : ObjectProperty C) (hG : (G ⊔ IsZero).triangEnvelope = ⊤) : F.essImage.IsTriangulated ∧ Nonempty F.essImage.IsStableUnderRetracts ∧ F.essImage = (G.map F ⊔ IsZero).triangEnvelope

reviewed_lean.note: Only the lean field changed; lean.statement is verbatim in the file. The hypotheses are faithful: C and D triangulated with free universes, IsIdempotentComplete C only, F Full+Faithful+CommShift+IsTriangulated, G an arbitrary ObjectProperty. Thickness is IsTriangulated (zero, shifts, extensions up to iso) plus IsStableUnderRetracts (which also gives iso-closure). (P ⊔ IsZero).triangEnvelope is exactly thick(P), by its retract and triangulated instances and triangEnvelope_le_iff; binary products are split extensions. So hG means thick(G)=C and the conclusion means essImage = thick(F(G)) via G.map F. Edge cases covered: empty G, zero categories, D not idempotent complete. No duplicate in side-live or Mathlib; no name or module collision. Docstrings carry the source place, blueprint tag and 5 steps; no hollow defs, proof is sorry only.
